summary_hint: whose rental property, at what address, leased to whom, for what monthly rent, over what term

typed_core.name: document_title
typed_core.why: identity/processor — distinguishes a residential lease from a commercial or month-to-month rental form; cheap review anchor

typed_core.name: issuer_name
typed_core.why: identity/source — form publisher (e.g. state realtor association) or property-management firm; validates the document is a real lease instrument

typed_core.name: landlord_or_lessor_names_raw
typed_core.why: disambiguator — verbatim lessor string so a bad split ('SMITH FAMILY TRUST AND JOHN SMITH') is visible to the tag layer

typed_core.name: landlord_or_lessor_name
typed_core.why: identity — DT-6/IN-14/OC-3 require the borrower to be the property owner/lessor to claim the rental offset/income; primary match key

typed_core.name: landlord_or_lessor_name_2
typed_core.why: identity — co-owner/second lessor (joint ownership of the REO)

typed_core.name: tenant_or_lessee_names_raw
typed_core.why: disambiguator — verbatim lessee string preserving an ambiguous split

typed_core.name: tenant_or_lessee_name
typed_core.why: identity — the paying tenant; processor confirms an arm's-length lease exists (IN-14 support)

typed_core.name: rental_property_address
typed_core.why: DT-6 (match to retained REO), IN-14, OC-3 (which property the rental income supports)

typed_core.name: unit_or_premises_description
typed_core.why: disambiguator for rental_property_address — which unit of a multi-unit building the lease covers, so it matches the correct REO line

typed_core.name: lease_start_date
typed_core.prompt_hint: Do not force effective/renewal dates into lease_start_date; use the operative lease term, and read the most recent amendment's rent if one supersedes the base lease

typed_core.name: lease_end_date
typed_core.why: proves the lease is still in force through closing; a lapsed lease weakens the rental-income support

typed_core.name: lease_term_type
typed_core.why: disambiguator — month-to-month vs fixed-term changes how IN-14/OC-3 treat the rental income
typed_core.prompt_hint: lease_term_type canonical values are not enumerated in the catalog; pass through the stated term type and normalize 'month-to-month' vs 'fixed-term'

typed_core.name: monthly_rent
typed_core.why: DT-6 (net-rental basis in DTI), IN-14, OC-3
typed_core.prompt_hint: Distinguish gross monthly rent (the lease figure) from any net/effective figure; put the stated contractual rent in monthly_rent and leave net-rental computation to the engine (DT-6 applies its own vacancy/expense factor)

typed_core.name: rent_due_date_or_day
typed_core.why: processor — confirms a normal recurring rent obligation vs an irregular arrangement

typed_core.name: security_deposit
typed_core.why: processor — presence of a real deposit is a signal of a genuine arm's-length lease (IN-14 authenticity)

typed_core.name: renewal_and_termination_terms
typed_core.why: processor — tells whether the lease auto-renews/continues past lease_end_date, affecting income durability

typed_core.name: landlord_signature_date
typed_core.why: execution — the lease is only binding support for IN-14/OC-3 once the lessor executes it

typed_core.name: tenant_signature_date
typed_core.why: execution — tenant execution completes the binding lease

rejected.name: form_number, form_revision_date
rejected.reason: a lease is not a standardized numbered form with a schema version

rejected.name: issuer_address, issuer_phone, issuer_email_or_url
rejected.reason: no rule/processor consumer; catch-all captures if present

rejected.name: document_issue_date, effective_date
rejected.reason: duplicate lease_start_date

rejected.name: expiration_date
rejected.reason: duplicates lease_end_date

rejected.name: statement_period_start, statement_period_end
rejected.reason: not a statement; duplicate the lease term

rejected.name: party_names, party_addresses
rejected.reason: generic; superseded by the specific landlord/tenant name fields

rejected.name: property_address
rejected.reason: generic; rental_property_address is the lease-specific field the rules read

rejected.name: loan_number
rejected.reason: not present on a lease

rejected.name: account_case_reference_number
rejected.reason: no cross-doc consumer for a lease

rejected.name: signature_blocks
rejected.reason: generic; superseded by landlord/tenant signature-date fields

rejected.name: notary_block
rejected.reason: residential leases are not notarized

rejected.name: document_status_or_version
rejected.reason: no consumer; draft/final rarely marked on leases

rejected.name: permitted_occupants
rejected.reason: no rule; occupant list not needed for income/DTI

rejected.name: other_deposits_or_prepaid_rent
rejected.reason: no rule consumer; catch-all

rejected.name: concessions_or_free_rent
rejected.reason: affects effective rent but no rule reads it in V1; engine uses stated monthly_rent

rejected.name: late_fees_and_returned_payment_terms
rejected.reason: no consumer

rejected.name: rent_increase_or_escalation_terms
rejected.reason: no consumer in V1

rejected.name: utilities_and_services_responsibility
rejected.reason: no rule; catch-all

rejected.name: maintenance_and_repair_responsibility
rejected.reason: no consumer

rejected.name: sublease_or_assignment_terms
rejected.reason: no consumer

rejected.name: property_management_agent
rejected.reason: no rule; not needed to establish income

rejected.name: electronic_signature_audit_data
rejected.reason: provenance-like; no consumer

rejected.name: lease_amendments_or_addenda
rejected.reason: see Open questions #1 — deferred, not adopted as typed core in V1

encoding_variations: Lessor/lessee labels vary — 'Landlord/Tenant', 'Lessor/Lessee', 'Owner/Resident', 'Management/Occupant'; the raw fields preserve the original wording for split-checking

Term type — stated as '12-month lease', 'fixed term', 'month-to-month', 'at will', or implied only by start/end dates; lease_term_type degrades from enum, so the prompt must map prose to a canonical value
Monthly rent — may appear as '$2,400', '2,400.00', or 'Rent: Two Thousand Four Hundred Dollars ($2,400)'; effective rent may be reduced by concessions/free-rent (captured only in catch-all in V1)
Property address vs unit — the building street address and the unit ('Apt 3B', 'Unit B', 'upstairs') may be on separate lines; unit_or_premises_description disambiguates

open_questions.q: Nested list — lease_amendments_or_addenda is CORE and can override monthly_rent/term
options: no list, read the operative terms into the flat fields
flat-row nested list {title, effective_date, changed_term, source}
open_questions.recommendation: no list for V1 — items are few/rare and the catch-all preserves the raw addendum; item count uncertain (usually 0-2), flag for Priya GEET'S DECISION (LP-438): BUILD IT — LP-437 made nested lists cheap (one declaration + the generic mechanism); the one-list-budget / defer / no-consumer concern is overturned. Build as flat_row; the per-rule consumer is separate follow-up.

options: str passthrough + prompt hint normalizing to {fixed-term, month-to-month, week-to-week, at-will}
open_questions.recommendation: str passthrough plus a prompt hint; add a coercer/enum later if a rule needs to branch on it

open_questions.q: REO matching — DT-6 must attach this lease to the correct retained property; rental_property_address + unit_or_premises_description is the only key
open_questions.recommendation: downstream address-match rather than a schema field

open_questions.q: Signature capture — flatten to landlord_signature_date/tenant_signature_date vs a signatures nested list
open_questions.recommendation: flatten — exactly two parties GEET'S DECISION (LP-438): FLATTEN signatures to signature_present + signature_date — no signature nested list.

open_questions.q: Third-party tenant PII — tenant_or_lessee_name (+ address via the raw string) is a non-borrower's PII at standard sensitivity
open_questions.recommendation: no _PII_FIELDS registration; confirm with Priya whether tenant identity should be masked GEET'S DECISION (LP-438): mask account-like identifiers (policy/account/plan numbers, wire/ACH trace, check references) via _PII_FIELDS; leave addresses and public-record case numbers PLAIN; DOB is unmasked (pii null).

notes: No existing_extractor for this document type — new schema.
This is an asset/income-support document: the borrower is expected to be the landlord/lessor, not the tenant. Capture the lessor names in landlord slots regardless of who signs first.
No fields require _PII_FIELDS registration in V1; party names and rental_property_address are standard sensitivity; there is no SSN/DOB on a standard lease.

landlord_signature_date and tenant_signature_date carry reason_class 'execution' in the doc, which is not one of the five classes; both were mapped to processor (execution/completeness) as a best guess — flagged as ambiguity.
